killedBy: hud.css is syntactically whole never centres the main axis of a pane that scrolls
why: The negative control for the OTHER half of the centred-axis sweep. That guard now asserts the centred set is EMPTY, and an empty list is what a sweep that measured nothing also produces -- so it pins the eight scrollers by name beside it. This mutation is what makes that pin load-bearing rather than decorative: dropping `overflow-y` from Settings removes it from the scroller population, leaves the centred set empty and therefore passing, and is caught only by the name list. It is also a real defect in its own right, since the pane is taller than a handset in landscape (measured at 844x390, where its content runs 536px) and would simply have its lower half unreachable.
